parsed.why: Decriminalisation (2025) removed conduct-based exposure; gender-neutral domestic-violence act protects visitors, police/port training documented. Violence evidence is dated, individual, orientation-based with no trans-specific data; negative UN vote is climate only. No traveler-facing restriction documented.

No criminalisation, hate-crime law covering gender identity, three LGBT centres, Prides, guide reports wide acceptance. Offsets: documented search difficulties for trans persons, uneven enforcement, escalating anti-gender disinformation, marriage ban via referendum, disrupted Pride — friction, not state threat.

Decriminalisation ruling under government appeal; immoral-acts provision still reaches same-sex displays; marriage recognition legislatively overridden; organised anti-gay political hostility. But pride marches and LGBT centre proceed, health rules bar discrimination, sodomy law unused since 1990. Contested rule of law lowers it.

Nationwide criminalisation (10–14 years), death penalty under Sharia in twelve northern states, documented police extortion for 'looking gay', mass hotel raids, app-based blackmail gangs, trans woman killed with impunity, official travel warning to LGBT travellers. State-tolerated targeting dominates.

Gender-identity discrimination criminalised since 2005, equality statute extended to services, conversion-practice prosecution, working parliamentary process, government defending trans travellers' documents. Recorded hate crimes rising but police-recorded with functioning reporting; border and facility questions unresolved rather than adverse.
